findings.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — New predicate clause `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` dereferences `idp.getConfig()` with no null-check; if getConfig() ever returns null for an org-linked IDP (e.g. a freshly-built model passed to create()/update() before its config map is initialized), this throws NPE instead of safely treating it as "not public broker".

server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:165 — getForLogin() (both the default interface implementation and the Infinispan-cached override) never filters out IdPs whose linked Organization is itself disabled — that check is only enforced via the isEnabled() override added by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(), so it only takes effect if the *caller* re-filters on idp.isEnabled() after the call (as the defensive `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() ...)` and "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped" comment in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80 shows); any future/alternate caller that trusts the getForLogin javadoc contract ("suitable for being displayed in the login pages") without adding this extra filter would display a login option for an IdP belonging to a disabled organization.

model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:77 — cacheKeyForLogin() keys the Infinispan cache entry only by (realm, FetchMode) and not by organizationId, so a single IdentityProviderListQuery object accumulates an unbounded searchKey->Set<String> map (one entry per distinct organizationId ever queried for getForLogin in that realm), causing unbounded memory growth of one cache value and ever-larger serialized payloads for realms with many organizations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — New predicate clause `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` dereferences `idp.getConfig()` with no null-check; if getConfig() ever returns null for an org-linked IDP (e.g. a freshly-built model passed to create()/update() before its config map is initialized), this throws NPE instead of safely treating it as "not public broker".

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new clause to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` when `idp.getOrganizationId() != null`. This is a new dereference chain with no null-check on `getConfig()`, so it can throw an NPE if `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` may ever be null. The diff itself does not show whether `getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null across implementations, so the risk is real but not verifiably a definite defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:165 — getForLogin() (both the default interface implementation and the Infinispan-cached override) never filters out IdPs whose linked Organization is itself disabled — that check is only enforced via the isEnabled() override added by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(), so it only takes effect if the *caller* re-filters on idp.isEnabled() after the call (as the defensive `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() ...)` and "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped" comment in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80 shows); any future/alternate caller that trusts the getForLogin javadoc contract ("suitable for being displayed in the login pages") without adding this extra filter would display a login option for an IdP belonging to a disabled organization.

adjudication.rationale: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin() only applies createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel() on the cache-miss/invalid path (`idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`), but on the cached path it returns `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` results directly without wrapping or filtering. The diff also updates OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean to defensively re-filter `idp.isEnabled()` with an explicit comment that the IdP “might have been wrapped”, indicating getForLogin() can yield IdPs that should not be shown on login unless callers add an extra filter. The added LoginFilter predicate also does not check linked-organization enabled/disabled state (it only checks orgId null or BROKER_PUBLIC), so getForLogin() itself does not enforce excluding IdPs whose org should make them unavailable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:77 — cacheKeyForLogin() keys the Infinispan cache entry only by (realm, FetchMode) and not by organizationId, so a single IdentityProviderListQuery object accumulates an unbounded searchKey->Set<String> map (one entry per distinct organizationId ever queried for getForLogin in that realm), causing unbounded memory growth of one cache value and ever-larger serialized payloads for realms with many organizations.

adjudication.rationale: The new getForLogin() cache key is only (realmId, FetchMode) via cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode), while the cached IdentityProviderListQuery is indexed by a per-request `searchKey` derived from `organizationId` ("" or orgId). When an organizationId is not yet present, the code rebuilds a new IdentityProviderListQuery by passing the previous query (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`), which implies it accumulates prior searchKey entries in a single cached value. With many distinct organizationIds queried over time for the same realm+mode, this single cache entry can grow without bound in-memory and in serialized size.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:428 — Test only exercises remove() on idp-alias-1, which is disabled and already non-qualifying for login, so cache invalidation on removal of a currently login-eligible IdP (the more important/likely path in production) is never verified

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()`, the only `remove()` exercised is `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-1").remove();`. Earlier in the test setup `idpRep.setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)`, so `idp-alias-1` is disabled and therefore non-qualifying for login. Meanwhile, the production logic added in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove()` now conditionally invalidates login caches via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which only triggers if `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` is true. The test verifies the “no invalidation when removing a non-login IDP” path, but does not verify invalidation when removing a currently login-eligible IDP (the new/important branch).
